title: The Line That Crosses the Fewest Bricks

concept.title: Count how many rows have an edge at each position
body: A wall has `n` rows of bricks, all rows with the same total width. You draw a vertical line from the top to the bottom. It crosses a brick unless it goes exactly along an **edge between two bricks** in that row. To cross as few bricks as possible, choose the position where **the most rows have an edge**. Edges at the very left and the very right of the wall are not allowed.

The position of an edge in a row is a prefix sum of the brick widths. The map counts, for every position, in how many rows an edge lies there. Skipping the last brick of each row leaves out the right border of the wall.

statement: A wall has `n` rows. Row `i` consists of `cnt[i]` bricks of height 1; all rows have the same total width. You draw a vertical line from the top to the bottom of the wall, which may not run along the left or right border of the wall. A line crosses a brick when it goes through the inside of the brick (an edge between two bricks is not crossed). Print the smallest possible number of crossed bricks.
The bricks are given as one list of `t` widths: first the bricks of row 1 from left to right, then the bricks of row 2, and so on.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `t` (the total number of bricks).
The second line has `cnt[1] ... cnt[n]`, the number of bricks of every row.
The third line has the `t` widths.
outputFormat: Print the smallest number of crossed bricks.
constraints: 1 <= each width, and the total width of a row is at most 10^9

examples.note: Row 1 has edges at 1 and 3, row 2 at 2, row 3 at 3. The line at position 3 runs along edges in rows 1 and 3 and crosses one brick in row 2.

hints: A line along an edge of a row does not cross a brick of that row.
The edge positions of a row are the prefix sums of its widths, without the last one.
Count how many rows have an edge at each position; the answer is n minus the largest count.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, t = map(int, input().split())
cnt = list(map(int, input().split()))
w = list(map(int, input().split()))

# Your code here

explanation: Every internal edge position (a prefix sum without the last brick) is counted in a map. The best line goes along the most popular position.
solution.complexity: Time O(t) on average, space O(t).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, t = map(int, input().split())
cnt = list(map(int, input().split()))
w = list(map(int, input().split()))

edges = {}
pos = 0
for i in range(n):
    s = 0
    for j in range(cnt[i] - 1):
        s += w[pos + j]
        edges[s] = edges.get(s, 0) + 1
    pos += cnt[i]
print(n - max(edges.values(), default=0))
